newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Wall Street factor chills Taiwan shares at close.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street factor chills Taiwan shares at close.

text.p: Taiwan's share index punched briefly through 9,000 points but failed to sustain the momentum, falling slightly at Tuesday's close as Wall Street's overnight plunge inspired local profit-takers, brokers said.
U.S. stocks tumbled on Monday after Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto set off waves of profit-taking with comments about potential sale of U.S. government securities by Japan.
Taiwan's index once hit 9,014.48 points but slipped to end at 8,918.17, a scant loss of 6.95 points or 0.08 percent.
Turnover, though brisk at T$169.4 billion, ended well below Thursday's all-time-high T$251 billion.
Brokers noted mixed viewpoints on whether the index would continue recent gains.
"After recent surges, some investors have turned cautious, but some others still are entering on hopes of more gains," said Lin Long-hsien, vice president of United Securities.
"This situation will continue in the coming sessions," Lin said.
Analysts said impact from Wall Street's tumble would be limited.
"Wall Street's fall should have little impact on Taiwan stocks," said HSBC James Capel research manager Alex Chen.
"Investors simply are using this as an excuse to take profits after the index's recent surge," said Chen.
Construction shares soared by 3.36 percent on a local newspaper report that ruling Nationalist Party-related businesses foresaw a sound outlook for construction shares.
"The government has in the past year released series of bullish news trying to boost the domestic property market, and the report was another try," Lin said.
